body:
The independent review is posted on BUG-2398 as the latest comment, if the queued store write lands. Summary:

VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED. Replace the keyring-pointer design (S1-S3) with a scoped Codex argv adapter.

What I proved (no model call, temporary CODEX_HOME, codex-cli 0.166.0):
1. codex sandbox applies inherit=core, even under danger-full-access. The parent's AIDA_* variables are dropped, so every managed Codex launch is affected, not only the native posture.
2. -c shell_environment_policy.set.<K>="v" MERGES with the user's set table. The user's existing keys survive and inherit stays core. The sketch's rejection 1 is wrong for an exact-key set. Inherit=all stays banned.
3. The keyring survives the codex sandbox wrapper.
4. The sketch treats the grant ID as a secret. It is not: authority needs key possession or ancestry.
5. A defect in the sketch: the subject check is circular. Under core, AIDA_USER is gone, so the caller becomes joe, which does not match the subject plan.name, and the result is SubjectMismatch.
6. S1 links the old keyring and so re-creates the parent-key exposure in new code.

Required contract (A1-A6 in the comment):
- One codex_tool_env_overrides() emits set.<K> for an exact const whitelist of non-secret AIDA child metadata, read from the child Command's own env: GRANT (UUID or ""), ROLE, USER, AGENT_NAME/TYPE, SESSION_ID, SCOPE, PROJECT_ROOT, AGENT_CONTEXT_FILE, POSTURE, HEADLESS.
- Never emitted: tokens, secrets, GRANT_FILE, CONTAINED.
- No resolver, keyring or pre_exec changes, and Claude argv is unchanged.
- A model-free codex sandbox preflight with booleans only.
- Actual-tool tests under core.

Unknowns: whether keyctl works under Codex's own bwrap/seccomp. It cannot be run nested from a Claude bwrap ("No permissions to create new namespace"), so the operator must run it from a host terminal. Also whether an exec with a model call behaves the same (operator-run fixture), and whether reviewer ancestry survives a PID namespace.

SECURITY FINDING TO FILE. I could not file it: aida add fails with "requirement ID allocation failed: Read-only file system".
Suggested title: A launched agent holds its parent's and other root grants' session keys, so it can present an advisor grant it was never given. Priority high; tags security, grants, keyring.

Evidence: /proc/keys in my live advisor child seat lists two possessor-only aida-grant keys (key names only were listed): my own grant 1df410e6, and root grant 05109bf2 (advisor, subject joe, delegable advisor/implementer/integrator/reviewer, bound proc+sid+key). 05109bf2 is NOT my parent; my parent is 4341ca93, which is bound to a process only.

Mechanism:
- grant_keyring sys::install KEYCTL_LINKs the previous keyring, and TASK-2195 reuse puts the keys of siblings from one launcher into a shared keyring.
- binding_overlaps matches ANY single token, so the key alone is enough.
- The subject comes from the AIDA_USER env var, which the caller controls.
- Grant IDs can be listed in ~/.aida/session-grants.

So a descendant can present an ancestor's root advisor grant. I did not exercise this. Fix direction: give each child a fresh keyring that holds only its own key and does not link the launcher's, or bind presentation to the keyring of record. That needs a sketch and an independent signoff.

Operator or upstream items:
- the U1 host probe
- the MCP approval_policy=never refusal of queue_done, which is the user's config and stays unchanged without an operator decision
- native write roots, which belong to STORY-2238
- the AIDA Codex bwrap backend, which does not exist yet (STORY-2238)
subject: BUG-2398 independent sketch review: CHANGES REQUESTED (scoped Codex -c set whitelist); separate grant-key exposure finding to file
